paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where “Base” denotes LLM without editing.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of knowledge probing on BioMedLM after applying different editing methods, as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 10³. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is linear and spans from 35% to 65%, with major gridlines every 5 percentage points. Six methods are compared: "Base" (black circles, solid line), "FT" (blue triangles, solid line), "IKE" (red triangles, solid line), "MEND" (brown diamonds, solid line), "MEMIT" (purple circles, solid line), and "ROME" (green squares, solid line). The "Base" method starts at approximately 38% accuracy and remains relatively flat, ending near 43%. "FT" begins at about 40% and increases to around 46%. "IKE" starts at roughly 43% and rises to about 49%. "MEND" begins at approximately 44% and increases to about 56%. "MEMIT" starts at about 43% and rises to approximately 54%. "ROME" shows the steepest increase, starting at around 51% and reaching approximately 65% at the highest co-occurrence number. All methods show a general upward trend in accuracy with increasing co-occurrence number, with "ROME" consistently outperforming the others across the range.
